program_overview.title: TMUA and STEP Preparation (Oxford MAT Now TMUA)
program_overview.tagline: School maths, used with real depth: reasoning about arguments for the TMUA, and long, careful written solutions for STEP.
program_overview.description:
Two tests now sit at the centre of UK university admissions maths. The first is the Test of Mathematics for University Admission (TMUA), run by UAT-UK. Its content specification says "The test will consist of two 75 minute papers, taken one after the other. Each paper will consist of 20 multiple-choice questions." Paper 1 is Applications of Mathematical Knowledge and Paper 2 is Mathematical Reasoning; there is "no formulae booklet", "Candidates may not use calculators", and there is "no penalty for incorrect answers". UAT-UK says the TMUA "is based on content typically covered within Higher Level GCSE mathematics courses or AS level mathematics", and that results are reported "on a scale from 1 (low) to 9 (high) to one decimal place". UAT-UK's 2027 entry course list names seven universities using the TMUA for some courses: Durham, Imperial College London, the LSE, Cambridge, Oxford, Warwick and UCL.

The Oxford Mathematics Admissions Test (MAT) has ended. Oxford's Mathematical Institute says: "The MAT will not take place, and all applicants for Mathematics or Computer Science (including joint honours courses) will take the TMUA instead." It describes the MAT as "a test used from 2007 to 2025". Oxford still publishes MAT past papers and solutions, and they remain fine problem-solving practice.

The second test is STEP, the Sixth Term Examination Paper, administered by OCR. OCR says STEP "is used by the University of Cambridge, the University of Warwick and Imperial College London", and Cambridge says STEP is used "as part of almost all conditional offers from Cambridge for" Mathematics. OCR's specification says STEP 2 and STEP 3 "will each be a 3-hour paper" of 12 questions: eight pure, two mechanics and two probability and statistics, each worth 20 marks, with candidates "assessed on the six questions best answered". OCR lists STEP 2 on 14 June 2027 and STEP 3 on 21 June 2027.

Cambridge itself says the TMUA "uses mathematics you will have already learned in your school studies, so there is no need to take a preparation course or to do much preparation beyond familiarising yourself with the test format". We take that seriously. This course is not a shortcut or a set of tricks: it is a place to do hard mathematics regularly with a teacher, to learn the logic and proof that TMUA Paper 2 tests, and to write the long, justified solutions STEP marks. Practice uses our own original problems, plus the free official materials (UAT-UK practice papers and Notes on Logic and Proof, Oxford's MAT archive, and STEP past papers and the Cambridge STEP Support Programme), which students use where they are published. We never copy official questions into our materials. We are independent of UAT-UK, OCR and every university, and we make no promise of scores, offers or places.
what_makes_this_different: Built around the 2027 entry reality: TMUA for Oxford and Cambridge maths and computer science, with the Oxford MAT archive kept as practice
Logic and proof taught directly for TMUA Paper 2: necessary and sufficient conditions, converses, counterexamples and finding the error in a proof
No-calculator, no-formula-booklet fluency, so the mathematics is fast enough to leave time for thinking
A STEP stage with full written solutions marked in detail, because OCR says marks may be lost if examiners cannot follow your working
Original problems for every topic, plus the free official papers used where UAT-UK, Oxford, OCR and Cambridge publish them
Honest about what preparation can do, quoting the universities' own advice, and never promising scores or offers

learning_path.phase_1: Fluency and depth in the TMUA content: algebra, functions, sequences, coordinate geometry, trigonometry, logarithms and calculus, without a calculator
learning_path.phase_2: Mathematical reasoning for TMUA Paper 2: logic of arguments, proof methods, counterexamples and identifying errors in proofs, then timed TMUA-style papers
learning_path.phase_3: STEP 2 and STEP 3: extended pure problems, mechanics and probability, full written solutions, timed 3-hour practice and the June 2027 papers

career_outcomes: Speed and accuracy in A Level pure mathematics without a calculator or formula booklet
A precise grasp of logical statements, implication and quantifiers
The ability to build, check and criticise a proof
Long, clear written solutions that an examiner can follow
Calm persistence on unfamiliar problems that take twenty minutes or more
A strong start for a mathematics, computer science, economics or physics degree

phase_1_tmua_content_fluency.title: PHASE 1: TMUA Content Fluency (Months 1-2, Weeks 1-8)
phase_1_tmua_content_fluency.description: UAT-UK's Section 1 knowledge, made fast and flexible without a calculator, and used in problems that do not look like textbook exercises.

week_1_2.title: Weeks 1-2: The Tests, a Diagnostic and Algebra Without a Calculator
topics: The TMUA and STEP in 2026 to 2027, which universities use them and what each paper tests
Why the Oxford MAT ended after 2025, and how its archive is still useful practice
A diagnostic of our own across GCSE and AS pure content
Indices, surds and rationalising denominators at speed
Quadratics: completing the square, the discriminant and what it says about roots
Starting an error log and a list of favourite techniques
projects: A personal starting profile: target tests, target universities and ten solved warm-ups
week_1_2.practice: Short original problems where the obvious method is slow and a better idea exists

week_3_4.title: Weeks 3-4: Polynomials, Inequalities, Sequences and Series
topics: The factor and remainder theorems, and algebraic division
Linear and quadratic inequalities, and inequalities with a parameter
Sequences from a formula and from a recurrence relation
Arithmetic and geometric series, and the sum to infinity
Binomial expansion for positive integer powers
Spotting structure: symmetry, substitution and a clever factorisation
projects: Write and solve five original problems that each hide a factorisation
week_3_4.practice: Timed sets at under four minutes a question (our arithmetic: 75 minutes for 20 questions)
week_3_4.assessment: Month 1 check: a timed set of original multiple-choice problems

month_2_geometry_trig_logs_calculus.title: Month 2: Coordinate Geometry, Trigonometry, Logarithms and Calculus

week_5_6.title: Weeks 5-6: Coordinate Geometry, Circles and Trigonometry
topics: Straight lines, parallel and perpendicular conditions
Circles in both forms the specification lists, and the circle theorems
Sine and cosine rules and the area of a triangle
Trigonometric graphs, identities and equations in a given interval
Exponentials and logarithms, and solving equations with them
Sketching graphs quickly and reading information from a sketch
projects: An original geometry pack where every answer starts from a careful sketch
week_5_6.practice: Graph-sketching drills: ten curves in ten minutes, checked in class

week_7_8.title: Weeks 7-8: Differentiation and Integration
topics: Differentiating polynomials and powers, tangents, normals and stationary points
Increasing and decreasing functions and second derivatives
Integration as the reverse of differentiation and as area
Definite integrals and areas between a curve and an axis
Using calculus to reason about a graph without drawing it precisely
Mixed problems where algebra, geometry and calculus meet
projects: A calculus problem set of our own with one written explanation per answer
week_7_8.practice: Mixed Paper 1 style sets of original problems, timed
week_7_8.assessment: Phase 1 assessment: a timed 75-minute set of 20 original multiple-choice problems

phase_2_mathematical_reasoning.title: PHASE 2: Mathematical Reasoning for TMUA Paper 2 (Months 3-4, Weeks 9-16)
phase_2_mathematical_reasoning.description: UAT-UK's Section 2: the logic of arguments and mathematical proof, taught from first principles and then tested under time.

week_9_10.title: Weeks 9-10: Statements, Implication and Quantifiers
topics: True and false statements, and the words and, or (inclusive) and not
If A then B, A if B, A only if B, and A if and only if B
Necessary and sufficient conditions, and how to tell them apart
The converse and the contrapositive, and which one is equivalent
For all and there exists, and negating a statement with quantifiers
Working through UAT-UK's free Notes on Logic and Proof alongside our own examples
projects: A logic glossary written in the student's own words with one original example each
week_9_10.practice: Original statements to classify as true or false, each with a reason or a counterexample

week_11_12.title: Weeks 11-12: Proof Methods and Counterexamples
topics: Direct proof and proof by cases
Proof by contradiction, including the irrationality of root 2 and the infinitude of primes
Disproof by counterexample, and choosing a good counterexample
Proof by induction, beyond the TMUA but needed later for STEP
What makes an argument valid even when its conclusion is false
Writing a proof so each line follows from the last
projects: Five short proofs of original statements, each written up twice: once rough, once clean
week_11_12.practice: Paper 2 style multiple-choice reasoning problems of our own, timed
week_11_12.assessment: Month 3 check: a timed reasoning set plus one written proof marked in detail

month_4_errors_and_timed_papers.title: Month 4: Finding Errors in Proofs and Timed TMUA Papers

week_13_14.title: Weeks 13-14: Identifying Errors in Proofs
topics: Dividing by something that might be zero
Squaring both sides and gaining false solutions
Assuming what was to be proved
Arguments that check a few cases and claim them all
Reversing an implication that only works one way
Locating the first incorrect line in a flawed argument
projects: Write three deliberately flawed proofs of our own design and swap them with a classmate to find the errors
week_13_14.practice: Error-finding problems of our own, each with the faulty line named and corrected

week_15_16.title: Weeks 15-16: Full TMUA-Style Practice
topics: Pacing two 75-minute papers taken back to back
When to move on, and why a guess is worth making when there is no penalty
Elimination, checking options and testing special cases in multiple choice
Using UAT-UK's free practice papers under timed conditions on UAT-UK's site
Using Oxford's MAT archive for longer problem-solving practice
Reviewing a paper: knowledge gap, method choice or slip
projects: Two full timed TMUA-style papers of our own, each followed by a written review
week_15_16.practice: One official free practice paper worked under timed conditions, reviewed in class
week_15_16.assessment: Phase 2 assessment: a full TMUA-style practice of two 75-minute papers of original problems

phase_3_step_2_and_3.title: PHASE 3: STEP 2 and STEP 3 (Months 5-6, Weeks 17-24)
phase_3_step_2_and_3.description: For students holding or expecting STEP offers: the specification's pure, mechanics and probability content stretched to STEP depth, and long solutions written in full.

week_17_18.title: Weeks 17-18: How STEP Is Built, and Pure Problems That Take Time
topics: OCR's STEP format: 3 hours, 12 questions, each worth 20 marks, with the six highest-scoring answers counted
STEP 2 built on A Level Maths and AS Further Maths pure content; STEP 3 on A Level Further Maths pure content, with OCR's additions
Choosing questions in the first ten minutes
Algebra and functions problems with several connected parts
Inequalities proved, not just solved
Using the earlier parts of a question to unlock the later parts
projects: Two long original problems written up in full, then rewritten after detailed feedback
week_17_18.practice: One STEP-length problem per class, about 30 minutes each

week_19_20.title: Weeks 19-20: Calculus, Series and Complex Numbers at STEP Depth
topics: Integration techniques: substitution, by parts and reduction formulae
Differential equations in context
Series, limits and careful approximation
Complex numbers and their geometry for STEP 3
Matrices and vectors as STEP uses them
Formulae OCR says candidates are expected to know, which go beyond the A levels
projects: A personal technique file: twelve methods, each with an original example
week_19_20.practice: STEP past papers worked from OCR's site and the Cambridge STEP Support Programme modules, reviewed in class
week_19_20.assessment: Month 5 assessment: a timed 90-minute half paper of original STEP-style problems

month_6_step_applied_and_june.title: Month 6: Mechanics, Probability and the June 2027 Papers

week_21_22.title: Weeks 21-22: Mechanics and Probability Questions
topics: Kinematics, forces and moments at STEP depth
Energy, momentum and collisions
Probability problems that need careful counting and conditional reasoning
Distributions and expectation in multi-part questions
Deciding whether an applied question suits you better than a pure one
Writing an applied solution: diagram, assumptions, equations and a conclusion
projects: Two applied problems of our own written up in full with diagrams
week_21_22.practice: Mixed long problems, one pure and one applied each week

week_23_24.title: Weeks 23-24: Full Papers and the June Sittings
topics: Full 3-hour practice papers under exam conditions
Clear, logical and legible working, as OCR's specification asks
Final review of each student's error log
OCR's 2027 dates: STEP 2 on 14 June 2027 and STEP 3 on 21 June 2027, with results on 12 August 2027
Registering through your school or college between 1 March and 4 May 2027
Moving on to university mathematics with good habits
projects: A final full paper reviewed one to one with the teacher
week_23_24.practice: Light, steady problem practice in the last week before each paper
week_23_24.assessment: Final assessment: a full timed STEP-style paper of original problems plus a short conversation about method choices

faqs.question: What is the TMUA?
faqs.answer: The Test of Mathematics for University Admission, run by UAT-UK. Its specification lists two 75-minute papers of 20 multiple-choice questions each: Paper 1, Applications of Mathematical Knowledge, and Paper 2, Mathematical Reasoning. There are no calculators and no formula booklet, and wrong answers carry no penalty.

faqs.question: Has the Oxford MAT been replaced by the TMUA?
faqs.answer: Yes. Oxford's Mathematical Institute says "The MAT will not take place, and all applicants for Mathematics or Computer Science (including joint honours courses) will take the TMUA instead." It describes the MAT as a test used from 2007 to 2025. Oxford's MAT past papers and solutions are still published and remain good problem-solving practice.

faqs.question: Which universities use the TMUA?
faqs.answer: UAT-UK's course list for 2027 entry names Durham University, Imperial College London, the London School of Economics, the University of Cambridge, the University of Oxford, the University of Warwick and UCL, for some courses in mathematics, economics or computer science. Requirements differ by course, and some list it as recommended rather than compulsory, so always check each university's own course page.

faqs.question: When is the TMUA?
faqs.answer: For 2027 entry, UAT-UK ran an October sitting from 12 to 16 October 2026, with booking closed on 28 September 2026 and results due on Monday 16 November 2026, and runs a January sitting from 4 to 8 January 2027. Most Oxford and Cambridge applicants must sit in October. Dates for 2028 entry will appear on UAT-UK's site.

faqs.question: Do I really need a preparation course for the TMUA?
faqs.answer: Cambridge says there is "no need to take a preparation course or to do much preparation beyond familiarising yourself with the test format", and UAT-UK publishes free practice materials. We agree that tricks are not the point. This course is for students who want regular, guided work on hard problems, logic and proof with a teacher, and it continues into STEP, which needs much more sustained practice.

faqs.question: What is STEP and who needs it?
faqs.answer: STEP is the Sixth Term Examination Paper, administered by OCR. OCR says it is used by the University of Cambridge, the University of Warwick and Imperial College London, and Cambridge says it is part of almost all of its conditional offers for Mathematics. There are two papers, STEP 2 and STEP 3, and offers usually name one or both.

faqs.question: How is STEP structured, and when is it in 2027?
faqs.answer: OCR's specification says each STEP paper is 3 hours with 12 questions: eight pure, two mechanics and two probability and statistics, each worth 20 marks, and only the six highest-scoring answers count. Calculators are not permitted. OCR lists STEP 2 on 14 June 2027 and STEP 3 on 21 June 2027, with registration through a school or college from 1 March to 4 May 2027.

faqs.question: Do I need Further Maths?
faqs.answer: For the TMUA, UAT-UK says the content is typically covered in Higher GCSE maths or AS level maths. For STEP, OCR bases STEP 2 on A Level Maths and AS Further Maths pure content and STEP 3 on A Level Further Maths pure content, so Further Maths matters a great deal for the STEP stage.

faqs.question: Do you use real past papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, where they are published, and on the publishers' own sites: UAT-UK's practice papers, Oxford's MAT archive, OCR's STEP past papers and Cambridge's STEP Support Programme. Our own class problems and mock papers are original and written by us. We never copy official questions into our materials.

faqs.question: Can you guarantee a high TMUA score or a STEP grade?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honest can. Results depend on the student, the paper and the work they put in. What we give is steady practice on hard problems, written feedback on proofs and solutions, and a monthly timed paper.

faqs.question: Are you connected with UAT-UK, OCR, Oxford or Cambridge?
faqs.answer: No. We are an independent online school and are not connected with or endorsed by UAT-UK, OCR or any university. Students register for the TMUA through UAT-UK and for STEP through their school or college, and should always check current dates and rules on the official sites.

faqs.question: How are the classes run, and can we try one?
faqs.answer: Live online classes, twice a week, with a real teacher, in a group batch of 15 to 20 students or 1-on-1. Weekdays or weekends, flexible: choose your batch, or for a very personalised plan choose 1-on-1 at your convenience, weekend mornings or weekdays. The first class is free, and there is no obligation to enrol.
